assumption: Legacy ratios were measured on another host (calibration.json: Intel Xeon @ 2.10 GHz; the K_0 / GF(2^23) row: Apple M4 Pro under load). The tuned ratio multiplies them by this host's R = ns_add_reference / ns_add_tuned and by the class (b) speedup F measured here, which assumes that (unit time) / (reference addition time) carries across hosts; derivation.<row>.units.<unit>.host_drift is this host's own ratio divided by the legacy one, and `sensitivity` summarises it.

fallback: An instance with no entry here keeps the factors measured on the host for that run, and the report names the units that fell back, so a row priced the old way says so.

flags.koblitz/K_0 / GF(2^23): legacy ratios from an Apple M4 Pro under load 30-150, not the Xeon of every other row

method: ratio_new = ratio_old x R / F; R = reference/tuned addition on this host (sweep), F = measured field speedup for class (b) units, 1 for class (c), class (a) unchanged. Generated by `gae-reference retable`.
unit: ns_per_<native unit> / ns_per_tuned_add, dimensionless (double stays a counted group operation)
what: Calibration ratios of the boundary ledger re-expressed in the tuned unit: nanoseconds per native operation divided by nanoseconds per tuned batched affine addition. Same schema as calibration.json; not read by Calibration::pin until the switch in research/tuned_gae_20261020/SWITCH_PLAN.md is made.
